title: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Combined Fire Severity
description:
Researchers at NASA Ames Research Center and the NASA Advanced Supercomputing Division created this combined fire severity product using observations from the Copernicus Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI). The multi-sensor approach combines Sentinel-1 sensitivity to structural changes in vegetation with Sentinel-2 sensitivity to spectral changes associated with burned vegetation to characterize fire-induced surface impacts.

The underlying analysis uses pre- and post-fire Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations to identify changes associated with fire severity. Sentinel-1 provides information about structural changes through variations in radar backscatter, while Sentinel-2 provides complementary information about vegetation condition from visible, near-infrared, and shortwave-infrared observations. The resulting classification represents a gradient of fire impact derived from the combined SAR and optical observations.

This product was developed for the January 2025 Southern California wildfires and should be treated as a rapid-response fire severity product. The classification is intended to support situational awareness and assessment of fire impacts to vegetation. Results are preliminary and should not be interpreted as a ground-validated assessment of structural damage.
